targetWords.definition: If you do something awhile, you do it for a short time.
targetWords.example: Wait here awhile, and I'll bring some tea.

targetWords.definition: Cyberspace is the imaginary place of the Internet where activities occur.
targetWords.example: I didn't receive your email. It probably got lost in cyberspace.

targetWords.definition: —- She asked her brother to edit her paper before she submitted it to her teacher.
An essay is a short piece of writing on a certain subject.
targetWords.example: She had to write a two-page essay for her English class.

targetWords.definition: To evaluate something means to study it, so a decision can be made.
targetWords.example: Joe and Ken evaluated the plan and agreed that it would work.

targetWords.definition: To faint means to go unconscious and fall down.
targetWords.example: Carol fainted because she hadn't eaten in over a day.

targetWords.definition: If something is global, it happens all around the world.
targetWords.example: Pollution is a global problem. gymnasium [d3 imneiziam] n.

targetWords.definition: -* When I go to the gymnasium, I use the treadmill for 20 minutes.
targetWords.example: When I go to the gymnasium, I use the treadmill for 20 minutes.

targetWords.definition: To highlight something means to mark it with a color so that it is easy to see
targetWords.example: I read my vocabulary list and highlighted the most difficult words.

targetWords.definition: If someone is ignorant about something, they have no knowledge about it.
targetWords.example: I'm a bit ignorant about his theories. Can you explain them to me?

targetWords.definition: An index is a list of words at the end of a book that gives information.
targetWords.example: If you look in the index, you'll find the right page number. lecture [lektfar] n.

targetWords.definition: -» His lecture on world hunger was very informative.

targetWords.definition: -* At the end of the story, Mother explained the moral to the children.
targetWords.example: At the end of the story, Mother explained the moral to the children.

targetWords.definition: To operate means to work or function.
targetWords.example: I'm sorry, but the trains are not operating today.

targetWords.definition: If something is private, it is only used by one person or group. — Don't look at my diary! It's private!
When something is recent, it happened a short time ago.
targetWords.example: I did not know what caused his recent behavior. resolution [rezalu:Jan] n.

targetWords.definition: -> At New Year, I made a list of resolutions to help me have a better year.

targetWords.definition: Jack is in his second semester of college.
If something is typewritten, it is written on a computer or typewriter.
targetWords.example: This is an important, formal project and must be typewritten.

targetWords.definition: When something is weird, it is very strange. My best friend's dad is a bit weird.

story.title: The Magic Computer
story.passage:
I had a difficult geography project to finish by the end of the semester. My teacher

wanted it to be typewritten, so I went to the school computer room. But when I got

there, all the computers were turned off. Apparently there was a recent problem, and

technicians were fixing it.

I knew of some private study rooms downstairs. They were small and dark, and the

computers were very old, but I had no choice. At least the computers were operating

correctly. I typed and highlighted the assignment's title: "Evaluate the Government's

Response to Global Warming." But I didn't know what to write in my essay. Finally I

decided to find a book to help me. I went to the library, checked the book indexes and

eventually found a useful book. Then I returned to the computer.

When I looked at the screen, I saw something so weird that I nearly fainted! The essay

was complete! Had somebody in cyberspace written it? I didn't know, but I was very

happy. I printed it out and handed it in. I got an "A."

After that, I used the computer for all my assignments. I'd type the title, wait awhile, and

the computer would do it. Every assignment was perfect; I never had to edit anything. I

stopped paying attention to my teacher's lectures and spent my extra time in the gymnasium.

And my grades got better and better.

A month later, I was walking into class when my friend said, "Are you prepared for the

test?"

"What test?" I asked.

"The geography test!" he replied. "I hope you studied. It's worth seventy percent of

our final grade!"

I failed the test, of course. I was completely ignorant about the subject.

After that, I made a resolution never to use the magic computer

again. The moral of this story is that if you cheat at

school, you won't learn anything.
